record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates training on fixed random pixel permutations and reports training and test accuracy, a conceptual test of whether networks fit unstructured inputs. Its other noisy-label results address a related setting but do not establish the claim versions about completely random labels or fitting noisy labels perfectly.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses random-label fitting and regularization in its introduction and prior-work section, citing Zhang et al.; those cited results are not this study's results. Its own random-pixel-permutation comparison is reported in Table 2. Other noise-level results are plotted, with text describing relative performance and overfitting.
record.test_reason: The standard-SGD control uses an architecture from Zhang et al., pixel permutations fixed per image, and training accuracy to test fitting unstructured inputs. The paper also measures fitting partially corrupted training labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that bilevel optimization improves generalization and reduces overfitting, especially with noisy labels. Their permuted-image experiment shows a smaller generalization gap, not successful perfect fitting.
record.recipe_differences: The pixel-permutation experiment follows the setup of Zhang et al. [36], but uses the study's bilevel optimizer alongside standard SGD and reports a different outcome measure emphasis: training and test accuracy and generalization gap. The original method is cited, not reproduced as a random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that noise-level performance varies by dataset and architecture; CifarNet improves consistently over SGD, while Inception gains are described for CIFAR-10 up to 70% noise and CIFAR-100 up to 50% noise. In the pixel-permutation experiment, bilevel optimization has a much smaller generalization gap than SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Bilevel optimization achieves 34.8% training and 33.6% test accuracy on independently permuted images, versus 50.0% and 33.2% for SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed bilevel optimizer reduces the generalization gap on permuted images.

record.problems: The random-pixel comparison is reported for one network and one input manipulation. It does not report uncertainty or a chance level. Noise-level results are shown in figures without recoverable numeric values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the label-noise sweeps in Figures 3 and 4: the supplied text gives only qualitative comparisons, and the plotted values cannot be recovered. These results do not establish the perfect training fit and steadily rising test error specified by V4; V4 is marked tested_not_extracted.

untested.parts: The text identifies 90% corruption on CIFAR-10 as completely random labeling, but the supplied figures contain no readable endpoint values establishing training fit or chance test accuracy. The unchanged-hyperparameter conjunction cannot be assessed.
Relative time to fit true and random labels, and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Shared pixel shuffling, Gaussian-noise inputs, and whether longer training reaches zero error.
A readable full corruption sweep establishing the shape of test-error degradation and fitting at every noise level.
Fitting completely random labels under weight decay, dropout and augmentation, and generalization after removing those regularizers.
The temporal order of learning shared real patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

missing.what: Standard-SGD training fit under 50% random label corruption: CifarNet training/test accuracy 96.75%/45.15%; Inception 65.06%/47.64%. Clean-label controls are 99.99%/75.68% and 99.91%/88.13%, respectively. These numeric results qualify the perfect-training-fit component independently of the declared omitted figure sweeps.

record.verdict_notes: The noise protocol replaces selected labels with other classes; 90% corruption on CIFAR-10 yields completely random labeling. Thus V1 is experimentally addressed, contrary to the record, but its outcome cannot be determined from the supplied figure text. The omitted sweeps are already declared in rows_left_out. Low training accuracy under the proposed mitigation should not be pooled with standard-SGD evidence against V3.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, chance test error, and whether this occurs without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training time to fit random versus true labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
The study tests fixed random pixel permutations only; it does not test shuffled inputs or independently permuted pixels, or report zero training error.

The study varies random label noise and reports training-label and clean-test accuracy in figures, but the supplied text does not give recoverable values establishing perfect training accuracy or steadily rising test error across the full range.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation permit fitting random labels, and whether removing them alone harms true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, and whether those labels are learned differently over training.
